facts.statement: Farm credit to individual farmers (including SHGs and JLGs of individual farmers and proprietorship firms of farmers) directly engaged in agriculture and allied activities covers: crop loans (including traditional and non-traditional plantations, horticulture and allied activities); medium and long-term loans (for example agricultural implements and machinery and developmental loans for allied activities); loans for pre- and post-harvest activities of own produce; loans to distressed farmers indebted to non-institutional lenders; loans under the Kisan Credit Card scheme; loans to small and marginal farmers for purchase of land for agricultural purposes; loans against pledge or hypothecation of agricultural produce, including warehouse receipts, for not more than 12 months, up to Rs 90 lakh against Negotiable Warehouse Receipts (NWRs) or electronic NWRs and up to Rs 60 lakh against other warehouse receipts; and loans for stand-alone solar agriculture pumps, solarisation of grid-connected pumps and solar power plants on barren or fallow land or in stilt fashion on a farmer's own agricultural land.

Farm credit to corporate farmers, farmer producer organisations or companies (FPOs/FPCs) of individual farmers, partnership firms and co-operatives of farmers: (a) crop loans, medium and long-term loans and pre- and post-harvest loans are eligible subject to an aggregate limit of Rs 4 crore per borrowing entity; (b) loans against pledge or hypothecation of agricultural produce for up to 12 months are eligible up to Rs 4 crore against NWRs or eNWRs and up to Rs 2.5 crore against other warehouse receipts; (c) loans up to Rs 10 crore per borrowing entity to FPOs or FPCs undertaking farming with assured marketing of produce at a pre-determined price; and (d) loans up to Rs 10 crore for purchase of the produce of members directly engaged in agriculture and allied activities. Urban co-operative banks may not lend to co-operatives of farmers.

Agriculture infrastructure loans are subject to an aggregate sanctioned limit of Rs 100 crore per borrower from the banking system. Ancillary services include the activities in Annex II item 2, loans up to Rs 50 crore to start-ups engaged in agriculture and allied services, and loans for food and agro-processing up to an aggregate sanctioned limit of Rs 100 crore per borrower from the banking system.

For the small and marginal farmer sub-target, small and marginal farmers (SMFs) include: farmers with landholding of up to 1 hectare (marginal farmers); farmers with more than 1 hectare and up to 2 hectares (small farmers); landless agricultural labourers, tenant farmers, oral lessees and share-croppers whose landholding share is within the SMF limits; SHGs or JLGs of individual SMFs directly engaged in agriculture and allied activities (banks keeping disaggregated data); loans up to Rs 2.5 lakh to individuals solely engaged in allied activities without a landholding criterion; and loans to FPOs, FPCs and co-operatives of farmers where the SMF landholding share is not less than 75 per cent, within the limits of paragraph 9.1 B.

All bank loans to micro, small and medium enterprises qualify for classification under priority sector lending, with the MSME definition as given in the MSME notifications; loans up to Rs 50 crore to start-ups that conform to the MSME definition are also eligible. With-recourse factoring where the assignor is an MSME is eligible, as is factoring through the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) (not applicable to RRBs and UCBs). Other eligible MSME-category loans include all loans to units in the Khadi and Village Industries sector (categorised as micro enterprises); loans to entities assisting the decentralised sector with inputs and marketing; loans to co-operatives of producers in the decentralised sector (not UCBs); loans by banks to NBFC-MFIs and other MFIs for on-lending to MSEs; loans to registered NBFCs (other than MFIs) for on-lending to micro and small enterprises up to Rs 20 lakh per borrower; and overdrafts to Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana account holders, categorised as micro enterprises.

Export credit (pre- and post-shipment, excluding off-balance sheet items) other than that classified under agriculture and MSME is eligible for priority sector classification as follows: for domestic banks, wholly owned subsidiaries of foreign banks, small finance banks and urban co-operative banks, incremental export credit over the corresponding date of the preceding year up to 2 per cent of ANBC or credit equivalent of off-balance sheet exposure (CEOBSE), whichever is higher, subject to a sanctioned limit of up to Rs 50 crore per borrower; for foreign banks with 20 branches and above, the same 2 per cent without the per-borrower limit; and for foreign banks with fewer than 20 branches, export credit up to 32 per cent of ANBC or CEOBSE, whichever is higher. These provisions do not apply to RRBs and local area banks. Education loans to individuals, including vocational courses, not exceeding Rs 25 lakh are eligible.

Housing loans to individuals for purchase or construction of a dwelling unit per family are eligible if they satisfy both a loan limit and a cost limit of the dwelling unit, by population of centre: centres with population of 50 lakh and above, loan Rs 50 lakh and dwelling unit cost Rs 63 lakh; centres with population of 10 lakh and above but below 50 lakh, Rs 45 lakh and Rs 57 lakh; centres with population below 10 lakh, Rs 35 lakh and Rs 44 lakh. Loans for repairs to damaged dwelling units are eligible up to Rs 15 lakh, Rs 12 lakh and Rs 10 lakh in the same three population bands, subject to the same dwelling unit cost limits. Housing loans to the bank's own employees are not eligible, and loans backed by long-term bonds exempt from ANBC are not classified. Bank loans to governmental agencies for dwelling units or slum clearance (carpet area up to 60 sq.m.) and bank loans for affordable housing projects using at least 50 per cent of FAR/FSI for dwelling units with carpet area up to 60 sq.m. are also eligible. Population is taken from Table A-04 of Census 2011 (urban agglomerations and towns); villages and rural areas use the band for population below 10 lakh.

Social infrastructure: loans up to Rs 8 crore per borrower for schools, drinking water and sanitation facilities (including household toilets and household water improvements), and up to Rs 12 crore per borrower for health care facilities in Tier II to Tier VI centres (for UCBs, centres with population below 1 lakh). Renewable energy: loans up to Rs 35 crore to borrowers for renewable energy based power generators and public utilities (street lighting, remote village electrification), and Rs 10 lakh per borrower for individual households. Others: microfinance loans given directly to individuals and SHG/JLG members that meet the Credit Facilities Directions criteria; loans not exceeding Rs 2 lakh to SHGs or JLGs for purposes other than agriculture or MSME; loans to distressed persons (other than distressed farmers indebted to non-institutional lenders) not exceeding Rs 1 lakh per borrower to prepay debt to non-institutional lenders; loans to State sponsored organisations for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes for inputs and marketing; and loans up to Rs 50 crore to start-ups engaged in activities other than agriculture or MSME.

Weaker sections is an overlapping category covering priority sector loans to: small and marginal farmers; artisans, village and cottage industries where individual credit limits do not exceed Rs 2 lakh; beneficiaries of government sponsored schemes such as NRLM and the Self Employment Scheme for Rehabilitation of Manual Scavengers; Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes; beneficiaries of the Differential Rate of Interest scheme; SHGs and JLGs; individuals and individual members of SHGs and JLGs availing qualifying microfinance loans; individual women beneficiaries up to Rs 2 lakh per borrower (the Rs 2 lakh limit does not apply to UCBs); distressed farmers indebted to non-institutional lenders; distressed persons other than farmers with loans up to Rs 1 lakh per borrower to prepay non-institutional debt; persons with disabilities; transgenders; and minority communities as notified by the Government of India. Overdrafts to PMJDY account holders within the Department of Financial Services limits may be classified as weaker section loans. Where a notified minority community is in fact in a majority in a State or Union Territory (Punjab, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Lakshadweep, Jammu and Kashmir), the minority item covers only the other notified minorities.

An enterprise is classified as a micro enterprise where investment in plant and machinery or equipment does not exceed Rs 2.5 crore and turnover does not exceed Rs 10 crore; a small enterprise where investment does not exceed Rs 25 crore and turnover does not exceed Rs 100 crore; and a medium enterprise where investment does not exceed Rs 125 crore and turnover does not exceed Rs 500 crore (the 21 March 2025 notification, in force from 1 April 2025, replaced the earlier figures of Rs 1 crore and Rs 5 crore, Rs 10 crore and Rs 50 crore, and Rs 50 crore and Rs 250 crore). A composite criterion applies: an enterprise that crosses the ceiling for its present category in either investment or turnover ceases to be in that category and moves to the next higher one, and no enterprise is placed in a lower category unless it goes below the ceilings for its present category in both. All units with GSTIN listed against the same PAN are treated as one enterprise and their investment and turnover are aggregated. Investment is linked to the Income Tax Return of the previous year (for a new enterprise without a return, a promoter's self-declaration is used until 31 March of the financial year in which the first return is filed); plant and machinery or equipment follows the Income Tax Rules and includes tangible assets other than land and building and furniture and fittings; exports of goods or services are excluded from turnover. Registration is online on the Udyam Registration portal on self-declaration, without documents, and gives a permanent Udyam Registration Number and an e-certificate.

facts.statement: Banks are mandated not to accept collateral security for loans up to Rs 20 lakh extended to units in the micro and small enterprise (MSE) sector, and are advised to extend collateral-free loans up to Rs 20 lakh to all units financed under the Prime Minister Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) administered by KVIC. On the basis of the good track record and financial position of the MSE unit, banks may raise the collateral-free limit to Rs 25 lakh as per their internal policy, and may use Credit Guarantee Scheme cover where applicable. Gold or silver pledged voluntarily by a borrower for loans within the collateral-free limit is not treated as a violation of the mandate. The amendment applies to loans to MSE borrowers sanctioned or renewed on or after 1 April 2026.

payload.title: Priority sector: farm credit limits
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Individual farmers** (and their SHGs/JLGs, and proprietorship firms of farmers) can get priority sector credit for crop loans, medium and long-term loans, pre- and post-harvest activities, distressed farmers' debt, **Kisan Credit Card** loans, **land purchase by small and marginal farmers**, and solar pumps and solar plants on their own land.

**Produce-pledge loans** (up to 12 months): up to **Rs 90 lakh against NWR/eNWR** and **Rs 60 lakh against other warehouse receipts**.

| **Corporate farmers, FPOs/FPCs, partnership firms, farmer co-operatives** | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Crop loans, medium/long-term loans, pre- and post-harvest loans | **Rs 4 crore** aggregate per borrowing entity |
| Produce-pledge loans (12 months) | **Rs 4 crore** (NWR/eNWR), **Rs 2.5 crore** (other receipts) |
| FPOs/FPCs farming with **assured marketing at a pre-determined price** | **Rs 10 crore** per entity |
| Purchase of **members' produce** | **Rs 10 crore** |

Urban co-operative banks **cannot** lend to co-operatives of farmers under this head.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The Rs 4 crore limit is an aggregate: several eligible loans to the same entity together cannot count beyond it.

self_check.prompt_text: A corporate farming company has crop loans of Rs 3 crore and a machinery loan of Rs 2 crore. How much counts under the Rs 4 crore aggregate limit?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Rs 4 crore at most; the excess does not qualify under that head.

payload.title: Agriculture infrastructure, ancillary services and small and marginal farmers
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Head | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| **Agriculture infrastructure** | **Rs 100 crore** per borrower from the banking system |
| **Food and agro-processing** | **Rs 100 crore** per borrower from the banking system |
| **Start-ups** in agriculture and allied services | **Rs 50 crore** |

**Who counts as a small or marginal farmer (SMF)**

- **Marginal:** landholding **up to 1 hectare**
- **Small:** **more than 1 and up to 2 hectares**
- **Landless** agricultural labourers, tenant farmers, oral lessees and share-croppers, within SMF limits
- **SHGs/JLGs** of SMFs (disaggregated data kept)
- Individuals **solely in allied activities**, loans up to **Rs 2.5 lakh**, with no land criterion
- **FPOs, FPCs and farmer co-operatives** where the **SMF landholding share is at least 75 per cent**, within the Rs 4 crore and Rs 10 crore farm credit limits
payload.expanded_explanation_md: SMF loans count towards the 10 per cent SMF sub-target and also qualify as weaker section lending.

self_check.prompt_text: A farmer holds 1.6 hectares. Marginal or small?
self_check.expected_takeaway: A small farmer (more than 1 and up to 2 hectares).

payload.title: MSME, export credit and education under priority sector
payload.core_explanation_md:
**MSME:** **all bank loans** to MSMEs qualify, plus start-ups that meet the MSME definition (up to **Rs 50 crore**). Also eligible: **with-recourse factoring** for an MSME assignor, factoring through **TReDS**, **Khadi and Village Industries** units (micro), producers' co-operatives in the decentralised sector, loans to MFIs for on-lending, and loans to registered NBFCs for on-lending to micro and small enterprises up to **Rs 20 lakh** per borrower. **PMJDY overdrafts** count as micro enterprise lending.

**Export credit** (other than agriculture and MSME):

| Bank type | Eligible |
| --- | --- |
| Domestic banks, WoS of foreign banks, SFBs, UCBs | **Incremental** export credit up to **2 per cent** of ANBC or CEOBSE (the higher), with **Rs 50 crore** per borrower |
| Foreign banks, **20 branches and above** | **2 per cent**, no per-borrower limit |
| Foreign banks, **fewer than 20 branches** | Export credit up to **32 per cent** of ANBC or CEOBSE (the higher) |

**Education:** loans to individuals, including vocational courses, up to **Rs 25 lakh**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Export credit to agriculture or MSMEs is counted in those categories instead, under their own limits.

self_check.prompt_text: Which type of bank may count export credit up to 32 per cent of ANBC?
self_check.expected_takeaway: A foreign bank with fewer than 20 branches.

payload.title: Housing loans under priority sector
payload.core_explanation_md:
A housing loan to an individual qualifies only if it meets **both** the **loan limit** and the **dwelling unit cost limit** for the **population of the centre**:

| Centre population | Loan limit | Max cost of dwelling unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **50 lakh and above** | Rs **50** lakh | Rs **63** lakh |
| **10 lakh to below 50 lakh** | Rs **45** lakh | Rs **57** lakh |
| **Below 10 lakh** | Rs **35** lakh | Rs **44** lakh |

**Repairs** to damaged dwellings: loan up to Rs **15 / 12 / 10** lakh in the three bands, within the same cost limits.

**Not eligible:** housing loans to the bank's **own employees**; loans backed by **long-term bonds** exempt from ANBC.

**Also eligible:** loans to **governmental agencies** for dwelling units or slum clearance (carpet area up to **60 sq.m.**), and **affordable housing projects** using at least **50 per cent of FAR/FSI** for dwelling units of carpet area up to 60 sq.m.

Use **Census 2011 Table A-04** population for the centre; **villages and rural areas** use the **below 10 lakh** band.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: Both tests must be met: a Rs 40 lakh loan on a Rs 60 lakh flat in a 20-lakh city fails the cost test.

self_check.prompt_text: A Rs 40 lakh loan on a flat costing Rs 60 lakh in a city of 20 lakh people: eligible?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No: the cost exceeds the Rs 57 lakh limit for that band, although the loan is within Rs 45 lakh.

payload.title: MSME classification under the 2025 notification
payload.core_explanation_md:
| Category | Investment in plant and machinery or equipment | Turnover |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Micro** | up to **Rs 2.5 crore** | up to **Rs 10 crore** |
| **Small** | up to **Rs 25 crore** | up to **Rs 100 crore** |
| **Medium** | up to **Rs 125 crore** | up to **Rs 500 crore** |

Set by **S.O. 1364(E) of 21 March 2025**, in force from **1 April 2025** (earlier figures: Rs 1 crore / 5 crore, 10 / 50, 50 / 250).

**Composite criterion**

- Crossing the ceiling in **either** investment **or** turnover moves the enterprise to the **next higher** category.
- It is placed in a **lower** category only if it is **below the ceilings in both**.

**Other rules**

- All units with **GSTIN under the same PAN** are **one enterprise**; investment and turnover are **aggregated**.
- Investment follows the **Income Tax Return of the previous year**; a **new** enterprise uses the promoter's **self-declaration** until 31 March of the year of its first return.
- Plant and machinery or equipment means tangible assets **other than land and building and furniture and fittings**.
- **Exports are excluded** from turnover.
- Registration on the **Udyam portal** by **self-declaration** (no documents) gives a permanent **Udyam Registration Number** and an e-certificate.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: This card replaces the earlier courseware-based card: the thresholds are now checked against the Gazette notification.

self_check.expected_takeaway: Small: turnover exceeds the micro ceiling of Rs 10 crore, so the enterprise moves up.

payload.title: Collateral-free loans to micro and small enterprises
payload.core_explanation_md:
**The mandate:** banks **must not take collateral** for loans **up to Rs 20 lakh** to **micro and small enterprise (MSE)** units. Banks are advised to give collateral-free loans up to **Rs 20 lakh** to all units financed under **PMEGP** (administered by KVIC).

**Optional extension:** on the unit's **good track record and financial position**, the bank may **raise the limit to Rs 25 lakh** under its **internal policy**. It may use **Credit Guarantee Scheme** cover where applicable.

**Voluntary pledge:** gold or silver that the borrower **pledges voluntarily** for a loan within the collateral-free limit is **not a violation**.

**From when:** loans to MSE borrowers **sanctioned or renewed on or after 1 April 2026**.
payload.expanded_explanation_md: The earlier limit was Rs 10 lakh; the amendment doubled the mandate.

self_check.prompt_text: May a bank ask for security on a Rs 18 lakh loan to a small enterprise sanctioned in May 2026?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No: collateral is barred up to Rs 20 lakh for loans sanctioned or renewed from 1 April 2026.

payload.title: Classifying enterprises under the composite test
payload.core_explanation_md: Classify each enterprise: (A) investment Rs 2 crore, turnover Rs 12 crore; (B) investment Rs 30 crore, turnover Rs 90 crore; (C) two units under one PAN, with investment Rs 8 crore and Rs 9 crore and turnover Rs 60 crore and Rs 70 crore; (D) investment Rs 130 crore, turnover Rs 300 crore.

worked_steps.description: A: investment 2 is within the micro ceiling of 2.5, but turnover 12 exceeds 10, so it moves up; check small ceilings (25 and 100).
B: investment 30 exceeds the small ceiling of 25, so it moves to medium; check 125 and 500.
C: aggregate the units under one PAN.
C: turnover 130 exceeds the small ceiling of 100, so it is medium (17 <= 125, 130 <= 500).
D: investment 130 exceeds the medium ceiling of 125, so it is above medium.

payload.final_answer_with_unit: A is small, B is medium, C is medium (aggregate Rs 17 crore and Rs 130 crore) and D is not an MSME

self_check.prompt_text: If A's turnover had been Rs 9 crore, what would its category be?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Micro: both investment (2 crore) and turnover (9 crore) are within the micro ceilings.

items.title: Priority sector: farm credit limits
items.core_explanation_md:
**Individual farmers** (and their SHGs/JLGs, and proprietorship firms of farmers) can get priority sector credit for crop loans, medium and long-term loans, pre- and post-harvest activities, distressed farmers' debt, **Kisan Credit Card** loans, **land purchase by small and marginal farmers**, and solar pumps and solar plants on their own land.

**Produce-pledge loans** (up to 12 months): up to **Rs 90 lakh against NWR/eNWR** and **Rs 60 lakh against other warehouse receipts**.

| **Corporate farmers, FPOs/FPCs, partnership firms, farmer co-operatives** | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Crop loans, medium/long-term loans, pre- and post-harvest loans | **Rs 4 crore** aggregate per borrowing entity |
| Produce-pledge loans (12 months) | **Rs 4 crore** (NWR/eNWR), **Rs 2.5 crore** (other receipts) |
| FPOs/FPCs farming with **assured marketing at a pre-determined price** | **Rs 10 crore** per entity |
| Purchase of **members' produce** | **Rs 10 crore** |

Urban co-operative banks **cannot** lend to co-operatives of farmers under this head.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The Rs 4 crore limit is an aggregate: several eligible loans to the same entity together cannot count beyond it.

self_check.expected_takeaway: Rs 4 crore at most; the excess does not qualify under that head.

items.title: Housing loans under priority sector
items.core_explanation_md:
A housing loan to an individual qualifies only if it meets **both** the **loan limit** and the **dwelling unit cost limit** for the **population of the centre**:

| Centre population | Loan limit | Max cost of dwelling unit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **50 lakh and above** | Rs **50** lakh | Rs **63** lakh |
| **10 lakh to below 50 lakh** | Rs **45** lakh | Rs **57** lakh |
| **Below 10 lakh** | Rs **35** lakh | Rs **44** lakh |

**Repairs** to damaged dwellings: loan up to Rs **15 / 12 / 10** lakh in the three bands, within the same cost limits.

**Not eligible:** housing loans to the bank's **own employees**; loans backed by **long-term bonds** exempt from ANBC.

**Also eligible:** loans to **governmental agencies** for dwelling units or slum clearance (carpet area up to **60 sq.m.**), and **affordable housing projects** using at least **50 per cent of FAR/FSI** for dwelling units of carpet area up to 60 sq.m.

Use **Census 2011 Table A-04** population for the centre; **villages and rural areas** use the **below 10 lakh** band.

items.title: MSME classification under the 2025 notification
items.core_explanation_md:
| Category | Investment in plant and machinery or equipment | Turnover |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Micro** | up to **Rs 2.5 crore** | up to **Rs 10 crore** |

| **Medium** | up to **Rs 125 crore** | up to **Rs 500 crore** |

Set by **S.O. 1364(E) of 21 March 2025**, in force from **1 April 2025** (earlier figures: Rs 1 crore / 5 crore, 10 / 50, 50 / 250).

**Composite criterion**

- Crossing the ceiling in **either** investment **or** turnover moves the enterprise to the **next higher** category.
- It is placed in a **lower** category only if it is **below the ceilings in both**.

**Other rules**

- All units with **GSTIN under the same PAN** are **one enterprise**; investment and turnover are **aggregated**.
- Investment follows the **Income Tax Return of the previous year**; a **new** enterprise uses the promoter's **self-declaration** until 31 March of the year of its first return.
- Plant and machinery or equipment means tangible assets **other than land and building and furniture and fittings**.
- **Exports are excluded** from turnover.
- Registration on the **Udyam portal** by **self-declaration** (no documents) gives a permanent **Udyam Registration Number** and an e-certificate.

items.title: Collateral-free loans to micro and small enterprises
items.core_explanation_md:
**The mandate:** banks **must not take collateral** for loans **up to Rs 20 lakh** to **micro and small enterprise (MSE)** units. Banks are advised to give collateral-free loans up to **Rs 20 lakh** to all units financed under **PMEGP** (administered by KVIC).

**Optional extension:** on the unit's **good track record and financial position**, the bank may **raise the limit to Rs 25 lakh** under its **internal policy**. It may use **Credit Guarantee Scheme** cover where applicable.

**Voluntary pledge:** gold or silver that the borrower **pledges voluntarily** for a loan within the collateral-free limit is **not a violation**.

**From when:** loans to MSE borrowers **sanctioned or renewed on or after 1 April 2026**.
items.expanded_explanation_md: The earlier limit was Rs 10 lakh; the amendment doubled the mandate.
